scope: English summary and two manuscript-only additions; the historical detailed correspondence is preserved unchanged.

entries.summary: Sharp asymptotic for the actual maximum Hamilton path count, with absolute uniform constants.
Original-angle Hessian identity, positivity and determinant formula. The present short Schur-complement proof is not mapped step by step.
Eventual unique carousel extremizers in all four blow-up models, with a common threshold for all base tournaments of each fixed odd order.
Strict monotonicity and limit of the regular-carousel constants.
Uniform permanent approximation for bounded doubly centred perturbations with a fixed operator-norm gap.
Summable weighted core-excess coefficients and first-excess estimate.
Complex permanent polarization and nonnegativity for positive semidefinite matrices.
Complete-homogeneous and geometric permanent bounds, retaining spectral multiplicities.
Gaussian recovery with the stated error budget and factorial second moment.
Local matrix scaling, including signed-input estimates and separate support/nonnegativity conclusions.
Displacement, capacity and mass-restored normalization bounds.
Gram-determinant deletion, centering and Lipschitz estimates.
Uniform paired Gaussian estimates for independent row and column deletion sets of equal size.
Small-score relative permanent approximation with uniform constants.
Positive determinant–permanent convolution for actual Hamilton path counts, including empty and singleton cases.
The cotangent operator bound and old C_* spectral bound have endpoints. The added bound rho <= (3n-1)/(n+1) < 3 has no new endpoint.
Tournament-matrix product comparison and suffix equality propagation.
Truncated-prefix comparison and equality rigidity.
Spectral extremality and signed-permutation classification, with a separate regular-carousel isomorphism bridge.
Integral sixth-moment deficit and quantitative spectral gap for regular non-carousel tournaments.
The old C_* auxiliary bound, NOT the current sharp-L Proposition 7.1.
Permanent variance bound, with the correct factor between degree variance and score variance.
Uniform small-score Hamilton path asymptotics for score bounds o(sqrt(n)).
Explicit odd carousel and even one-vertex-deletion path counts attain L + O(1/n).
Analytic original-coordinate branch and its Hessian. The current short alternative derivation is not mapped step by step.
Actual path/cycle expectation limits in uniform and regular models, and their ratios.
Determinant, spectral-ratio and regular-carousel constant closed forms.
The same discrete odd-order monotonicity and limit as Corollary 1.5.
The same four-model eventual extremizer conclusion as Corollary 1.4.
Fair random augmentation identities and normalized expectation bridges; the order-one exception is retained.
The sharp maximum endpoints imply the same uniform upper bound; the present 5.2 -> 6.6 -> 7.3 -> 7.1 proof chain is not mapped.
Weighted convolution moments and the uniform long-deletion tail have no new endpoint.
Existing spectral and closed-form components do not constitute a mapped endpoint for this all-order composition.
The score-sensitive upper bound retaining exp(-tau/2 + K_1/n) has no new endpoint; a global sharp bound does not substitute for it.
Degree stability V_deg <= C(epsilon*n^2+n), and O(n) variance for exact maximizers, have no new endpoint. This does not assert regularity, edit-distance stability or carousel isomorphism.
For even n, every tournament has V_deg >= n/4 by integrality of outdegrees. Together with Corollary 8.3 this gives V_deg = Theta(n) for exact maximizers. No new Lean endpoint.
With delta=(P(n)-H(T))/mu_n, absolute C,N work uniformly for n>=N and 0<=delta<=(L-1)/4: V_deg(T)<=C(delta*n^2+n). In particular an O(mu_n/n) count gap gives O(n) variance. No new Lean endpoint.
